As part of the investigation into Power Station No. 3, the Militia retains the hypothesis of a network that manufactures false alibis by tampering with time clocks.

Viktor ADLER, 72, repairer, Block 7, District 2, has been arrested. Seized: a handwritten notebook of times and a shortwave radio set. A man who notes the comings and goings of an entire building and listens to foreign stations is no mere clockmaker.

"Little VOSK. I watched you grow up on the stairs. Look where you're sitting now.

Your father came to see me in March '71. Not about his clock — with questions. He wanted to know who set the ministry's clocks, and why some ran slow on the evenings of arrests. He put his clock down on my workbench and said he'd come back for it. He was never seen again.

The times, I write them down to protect people, not to lose them. I covered for you too. Do what you like with that."

Viktor ADLER est un vieux réparateur d'h: Viktor ADLER is an old clock repairer from Block 7, VOSK's neighbour, who has been noting the building's times since 1974 — partly for THE TRUE HOUR network, which protects people by adjusting clocking-in times, partly out of a caretaker's habit. He has nothing to do with the explosion. The round-up of clockmakers is looking for a convenient culprit for the sabotage; ADLER is one.
